items.text: Of the common acids in the lab, nitric acid has much more complex reactions with metals. You won't be asked about this at International GCSE.

items.label: text
items.text: Sulfuric acid can be thought of as the parent acid of all the sulfates (the salts formed from sulfuric acid are all called sulfates). It doesn't matter if the replacement of the hydrogen can't be done directly. For example, you can't make copper(ll) sulfate from copper and dilute sulfuric acid because they don't react. There are, however, other ways of making it from sulfuric acid – copper(Il) sulfate is still a salt.

items.label: text
items.text: Salts are also formed when the hydrogen in an acid is replaced with NH. These are ammonium salts, for example NH4Cl (ammonium chloride) and (NH4)2SO4(ammonium sulfate).

items.label: section_header
items.text: REACTIONS OF ACIDS

items.label: text
items.text: Before we look at some practical methods to make salts, we need to study the reactions of acids.

items.label: text
items.text: Simple dilute acids react with metals depending on their positions in the reactivity series.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Metals below hydrogen in the series don't react with dilute acids.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Metals above hydrogen in the series react to produce hydrogen gas.

items.label: list_item
items.text: The higher the metal is in the reactivity series, the more vigorous the reaction. You would never mix metals such as sodium or potassium with acids because their reactions are too violent.

items.text: A summary equation for metals above hydrogen in the reactivity series:

items.text: REACTIONS INVOLVING MAGNESIUM AND ACIDS

items.label: text
items.text: There is rapid fizzing and a colourless gas is evolved, which pops with a lighted splint (the test for hydrogen). The reaction mixture becomes very warm as heat is produced. The magnesium gradually disappears to leave a colourless solution of magnesium sulfate.

items.label: formula
items.text: M g ( s ) + H _ { 2 } S O _ { 4 } ( a q ) \rightarrow M g S O _ { 4 } ( a q ) + H _ { 2 } ( g )

items.label: text
items.text: This is a displacement reaction. The more reactive magnesium has displaced the less reactive hydrogen.
